claims.notes: [BATCH NOTE b084] Scope for this batch is lines 1-131 only (a sibling agent covers 132-247). Scope decisions: Obs identifiers (Obs 301, Obs 302), condition/run names (T=0.3, T=0.7, image (T=0.7), text-MIN), map-sheet names (K-35-067-2, K-35-054-2_Atolov_4326, the '1981' in 'Russian1981_32635', etc.) and numbers inside file paths are out of C4 scope per instrument rule 5. The '(50, 75] m' shell bounds are extracted once at line 3 as the analysis parameter actually run; the repeat at line 35 is treated as a shell identifier. The quoted column label "Runs in top-3" (line 81) and the 'Top-3 in' table header (line 86) are names; the selection rule 'top-3 per run' (line 55) IS extracted. Positional descriptors ('mountainous L half', 'forest L portion') are qualitative, not quantities. The '0' in 'gdal_translate -outsize 2048 0' is gdal's auto-height sentinel, not an asserted quantity. SCALE CONVENTION: this document quotes shell rates as percentages while the anchor artefact results/55maps-per-map-shell-variance/per_map_shell_rates.json stores them as fractions (0.75 for '75.00 %'); every such value carries unit '%' per instrument v1.2 amendment 6 so the harness can bridge the scale. MAX-RATE CONVENTION: the comparison table's 'Max rate' column is defined at line 81 as the maximum across the four runs, so each row is emitted as arithmetic with expression '100 * max(a, b, c, d)' over the four per-run shell_rate operands; if the harness cannot evaluate max(), every per-run operand path is present for triage. Preview PNGs are not committed and inputs/rasters/Russian1981_32635/*.tif is present on disk but untracked ('git ls-files inputs/rasters/' returns nothing), so preview-resolution and raster-size claims are anchor-unknown. Claim-specific: the 3–4 % corpus-rate endpoints are rounded summaries over the three text-track runs (t0.3, t0.7, text-min) — the minimum and maximum text-track corpus_rate paths are given, but the endpoints are quoted to whole percent so triage owns the rounding tolerance. The median, the 'three of four runs' count, the '2–3 maps' count and the 33–75 % rate range are all aggregations over $.runs[*].per_map[*].shell_rate and are marked recompute-script rather than pinned to a single locator.
